say.en: Dip a zinc strip into blue copper sulphate solution and it gets coated with copper. Keep the zinc and the copper ions apart, join them with a wire, and the same reaction drives a current. In this lesson: Describe the Daniell cell and the role of the salt bridge.
Write cell notation.
Calculate E degreescell from standard electrode potentials.

body.en: A galvanic (voltaic) cell turns the Gibbs energy of a spontaneous redox reaction into electrical energy. In the *Daniell cell*, Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s). Zinc is oxidised at the anode (negative), Cu²⁺ is reduced at the cathode (positive), and a salt bridge joins the two solutions. With 1 M ions the emf is 1.1 V. The cell is written Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(aq) || Cu²⁺(aq) | Cu(s): anode on the left, cathode on the right.
body.kn: ಗ್ಯಾಲ್ವಾನಿಕ್ ಕೋಶವು ಸ್ವಯಂಪ್ರೇರಿತ ರೆಡಾಕ್ಸ್ ಕ್ರಿಯೆಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಶಕ್ತಿಯಾಗಿ ಬದಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಡೇನಿಯಲ್ ಕೋಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಸತು ಆನೋಡ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಉತ್ಕರ್ಷಣಗೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ, ತಾಮ್ರದ ಅಯಾನು ಕ್ಯಾಥೋಡ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಅಪಕರ್ಷಣಗೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ, ಲವಣ ಸೇತುವೆ ಎರಡು ದ್ರಾವಣಗಳನ್ನು ಜೋಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Two beakers: a zinc rod in zinc sulphate and a copper rod in copper sulphate, joined by a wire through a voltmeter and by a salt bridge.

body.en: Each half-cell has an *electrode potential*. It is measured against the standard hydrogen electrode, Pt | H₂(1 bar) | H⁺(1 M), which is given 0.00 V. By convention we list reduction potentials. The more positive E°, the stronger the oxidising agent; the more negative E°, the stronger the reducing agent. The emf of a cell is the difference of the two reduction potentials.

myth.en: For $2\text{Ag}^+ + 2e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Ag}$, I must double $E^\circ$ to $1.60$ V.

truth.en: $E^\circ$ stays 0.80 V whatever coefficients you use. Electrode potential is an intensive property. Learners treat E° like ΔH, which does scale with the amount. Potential is energy per unit charge, so doubling both the energy and the charge leaves it unchanged.

say.en: A galvanic cell turns the energy of a spontaneous redox reaction into electricity; oxidation at the anode, reduction at the cathode.

SHE is the reference ($E^\circ = 0$). $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}}$, using reduction potentials.
Higher $E^\circ$: stronger oxidising agent. Lower $E^\circ$: stronger reducing agent. $E^\circ$ does not scale with coefficients.

problem.en: E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V and E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V. Find E° of the Daniell cell and say which electrode is the anode.

steps.en: Zinc has the lower (more negative) reduction potential, so zinc is oxidised: Zn is the anode.
E°cell = 1.10 V, positive, so the reaction is spontaneous.

answer.en: E°cell = 1.10 V; zinc is the anode

narration.en: Let us solve this together. E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V and E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V. Find E° of the Daniell cell and say which electrode is the anode.

say.en: Let us solve this together. E degrees(Zn squared⁺/Zn) equals minus 0.76 volts and E degrees(Cu squared⁺/Cu) = plus 0.34 volts. Find E degrees of the Daniell cell and say which electrode is the anode.
Zinc has the lower more negative reduction potential, so zinc is oxidised: Zn is the anode.
E degreescell equals E degreescathode - E degreesanode equals 0.34 - minus 0.76.
E degreescell equals 1.10 volts, positive, so the reaction is spontaneous.
So the answer is E degreescell equals 1.10 volts; zinc is the anode.

problem.en: E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V and E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = +0.80 V. Write the cell and find its E° for Cu + 2Ag⁺ → Cu²⁺ + 2Ag.

steps.en: Copper is oxidised (lower E°), so it is the anode on the left: Cu | Cu²⁺ || Ag⁺ | Ag.
We do not double 0.80 V for 2Ag⁺: electrode potential does not depend on the amount.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V and E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = +0.80 V. Write the cell and find its E° for Cu + 2Ag⁺ → Cu²⁺ + 2Ag.

say.en: Let us solve this together. E degrees(Cu squared⁺/Cu) = plus 0.34 volts and E degrees(Ag⁺/Ag) = plus 0.80 volts. Write the cell and find its E degrees for Cu plus 2Ag⁺ gives Cu squared⁺ plus 2Ag.
Copper is oxidised lower E degrees, so it is the anode on the left: Cu | Cu squared⁺ || Ag⁺ | Ag.
E degreescell equals 0.80 minus 0.34 equals 0.46 volts.
We do not double 0.80 volts for 2Ag⁺: electrode potential does not depend on the amount.
So the answer is 0.46 volts.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. A galvanic cell converts the Gibbs energy of a redox reaction into electrical energy.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ಗ್ಯಾಲ್ವಾನಿಕ್ ಕೋಶ ರೆಡಾಕ್ಸ್ ಕ್ರಿಯೆಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಶಕ್ತಿಯಾಗಿ ಬದಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Anode: oxidation, negative. Cathode: reduction, positive.
say.kn: ಆನೋಡ್: ಉತ್ಕರ್ಷಣ, ಋಣ. ಕ್ಯಾಥೋಡ್: ಅಪಕರ್ಷಣ, ಧನ.

say.en: E degreescell equals E degreescathode - E degreesanode, measured against SHE equals 0 volts.
say.kn: E degreesಕೋಶ equals E degreesಕ್ಯಾಥೋಡ್ - E degreesಆನೋಡ್; SHE ವಿಭವ ಶೂನ್ಯ.

say.en: More negative E degrees means a stronger reducing agent.
say.kn: ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಋಣ E degrees ಎಂದರೆ ಪ್ರಬಲ ಅಪಕರ್ಷಕ.

say.en: Next: Nernst equation, Gibbs energy and equilibrium constant.
say.kn: ಮುಂದೆ: ನರ್ನ್ಸ್ಟ್ ಸಮೀಕರಣ, ಗಿಬ್ಸ್ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸಮತೋಲನ ಸ್ಥಿರಾಂಕ.
